label: Week of 23 November 2026
summary: Guru Nanak’s 557th Parkash Purab is the week. Harmandir Sahib is lit. The jatha is at Nankana Sahib. Kartarpur is still shut. Five hundred pilgrims never made the gate.

items.headline: Guru Nanak’s 557th Parkash Purab fills Harmandir Sahib
items.dek: The Guru’s day. Ishnan in the sarovar. Kirtan at Sri Harmandir Sahib and at Ber Sahib, Sultanpur Lodhi. Langar wherever the Nishan Sahib stands. A nagar kirtan left the Akal Takht on Sunday under the canopy of Guru Granth Sahib. Deepmala tonight. This is the Panth, in public — not a greeting card.
items.imageAlt: Sri Harmandir Sahib at night, Amritsar

items.headline: 2,339 Indian Sikhs at Nankana Sahib for the Guru’s parkash
items.dek: The main diwan is at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, the birthplace. 2,339 pilgrims crossed Attari–Wagah on 22 November; 1,822 of them in the SGPC jatha led by Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargaj. Pakistan had issued 3,091 visas. Akhand Path. Nagar kirtan. The gate that opened was the old one, with a visa stamped in it.
items.imageAlt: Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, at dusk

items.headline: Kartarpur is shut on Guru Nanak’s day
items.dek: The visa-free corridor to the Guru’s last home has been closed since May 2025. On Parkash Purab it is still closed. Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargaj, leading the jatha, asked India and Pakistan to reopen it and to give Sikhs visa-on-arrival. The jatha will reach Kartarpur on 27 November by road, through Pakistan. The short walk from Dera Baba Nanak is a file.
items.imageAlt: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, Guru Nanak’s last home

items.headline: Five hundred pilgrims missed Nankana Sahib. The visas came late.
items.dek: Pakistan approved 3,091 visas. 2,339 crossed. Around 500 never reached Attari in time: passports came back after 20 November, some from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Bihar. The 1974 protocol is a dated entry, not a window. Miss the crossing and the rest of the visa is paper. The DSGMC protested at the High Commission in Delhi.
items.imageAlt: A Sikh jatha taking blessing at the Akal Takht, about 1924

items.headline: The Akal Takht panel will not sit until the Satkar Act is stayed
items.dek: Punjab’s Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 is in dispute. The Takht’s expert panel skipped the government’s meeting on Monday. It will not talk until the Act is stayed, as the Takht ordered. The government has asked again for 27 November. The question is the Guru’s book, and who writes the law around it.
items.imageAlt: Takht Sri Hazur Sahib, Nanded, where the Guru vested authority in the Granth

label: Week of 16 November 2026
summary: A Manhattan court sentenced a man to nineteen years for the plot to kill a Sikh on American soil. Bhai Amritpal Singh, MP for Khadoor Sahib, was brought out of Dibrugarh for three hours, then sent back. Guru Nanak’s parkash is days away. Kartarpur is still shut.

items.headline: Nineteen years for the plot to kill a Sikh on American soil
items.dek: A Manhattan federal court sentenced Nikhil Gupta to 235 months — nineteen years and seven months — for a murder-for-hire plot against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a U.S. citizen and Sikh political activist. The U.S. Department of Justice said Gupta worked at the direction of an Indian government employee. India denies involvement. The target was a Sikh. The sentence is on the record.
items.imageAlt: Nishan Sahib at Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar

items.headline: Bhai Amritpal Singh was brought out of Dibrugarh — for three hours
items.dek: The Khadoor Sahib MP, held in Assam since 2023, was taken under escort to Jallupur Khera to attend Mata Charan Kaur’s cremation. The court allowed noon to 3 p.m. He did not address the sangat. By 2:35 p.m. police had him on the road back to Amritsar airport and Dibrugarh Central Jail. An MP. A funeral. Then the same cell.
items.imageAlt: A Sikh jatha taking blessing at the Akal Takht, about 1924

items.headline: 3,091 Indian Sikhs cleared for Nankana Sahib
items.dek: Pakistan issued visas for Guru Nanak’s 557th parkash. The jatha crosses Wagah on 22 November. The main diwan is at Gurdwara Janam Asthan on the 24th. Kartarpur is on the itinerary for the 27th — by road, because the corridor is still closed.
items.imageAlt: Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, at dusk

items.headline: Kartarpur is still shut. Prakash Purab is this week.
items.dek: The visa-free corridor to Guru Nanak’s last home has been closed since May 2025. A BJP spokesman said it may reopen when the border is ‘conducive’ — and gave no date. The Akal Takht Jathedar and the SGPC asked that it be opened for this parkash. The sangat prays for darshan. The gate is a policy.
items.imageAlt: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, Guru Nanak’s last home

items.headline: Harjinder Singh Dhami elected SGPC president for a sixth term
items.dek: Unanimous, at Teja Singh Samundri Hall, in the presence of Guru Granth Sahib. 112 members sat. He named a Sikh centre in the United States, the Ravidas centenary, and Amritsar’s 450th year. The house then turned to prisoners, Kartarpur, and a capital still withheld.
items.imageAlt: The Akal Takht and Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar

label: Weeks of 2–9 November 2026
summary: The 1984 Sikh genocide’s anniversary. Bandi Chhor Divas. Survivors said justice has not come. The Jathedar said the prisoners have not come out. November is not a commemoration only.

items.headline: SGPC president: the scars of 1984 are still fresh. Justice has not come.
items.dek: Harjinder Singh Dhami called the November killings a blot on the largest democracy, carried out with the patronage of the then Congress government. Families still wait. SikhHub records those days as the 1984 Sikh genocide. The Nand Nagri affidavits are in this archive.
items.imageAlt: Widows of Sikhs killed in Delhi during the 1984 Sikh genocide

items.headline: On Bandi Chhor Divas the Jathedar asked for the Bandi Singhs
items.dek: From the Darshani Deori, Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargaj tied Guru Hargobind’s release of 52 kings to the prisoners still held. If governments will not act, he said, the SGPC must plan with the Panth. He also asked for Kartarpur to be opened.
items.imageAlt: Sri Harmandir Sahib at night, Amritsar

items.headline: Survivors said, again, that 1984 has no accounting
items.dek: Nirpreet Kaur and Atma Singh Lubana spoke at a Punjab meeting on the 42-year delay. H. S. Phoolka recalled Nanavati, Sajjan Kumar, Jagdish Tytler. SikhHub does not take a party’s platform as the verdict. The Delhi High Court already named crimes against humanity. The papers follow.
items.imageAlt: A Sikh woman in Punjab holding a painted portrait of a disappeared relative
